title: Greedy-Seeded Swarm Metaheuristics for Multi-UAV Disaster Search over CNN-Derived Priority Maps: A Budget-Matched Simulation Study
content: Battery-limited drone fleets must decide where to search first after an earthquake or flood. We study this decision in a reproducible simulation: a compact convolutional neural network (SARNet) turns a synthetic reconnaissance image into a per-cell search-priority map, and planners route five drones over that map to maximise a time-discounted search value. Four swarm metaheuristics—particle swarm optimization (PSO), a MAX–MIN ant system (ACO), the firefly algorithm (FA) and the grey wolf optimizer (GWO)—and two greedy-seeded variants are compared with random search, a lawnmower sweep and a greedy heuristic under an identical budget of 3,000 objective evaluations, on 20 scenarios, using Friedman and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. No pure swarm algorithm significantly outperformed the greedy heuristic. Seeding PSO with four greedy plans raised the mean detection rate to 76.9% (greedy: 72.4%; lawnmower: 24.1%) and gave the highest objective value in all 20 scenarios (all pairwise Holm-adjusted p ≤ 0.006). With an identical seeded initial population, GWO never improved on its best initial plan, whereas PSO improved the mean objective by 9.4. A map-source ablation shows that the learned map drives most of the gain (28–37% detection with a uniform map), and a scalability study shows that the seeded PSO led in five of six settings while ACO led on 30×30 maps. The detector reaches 96.2% accuracy on held-out patches from the same synthetic renderer, which says little about real imagery; the study involves no flight hardware or real disaster data.
